newsitem.title: INDIA: Mandela sees no hitches to Indian Ocean trade bloc.
newsitem.headline: Mandela sees no hitches to Indian Ocean trade bloc.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela said at the start of a visit to India on Thursday that tensions between India and Pakistan should not derail efforts for free trade in an Indian Ocean bloc.
"I have confidence in the leadership of India and Pakistan," Mandela told reporters in response to a question after a reception for his three-day visit.
Tension between India and Pakistan over the disputed Kashmir region has been seen as a sticking point in efforts for free trade in an Indian Ocean bloc first proposed by South Africa.

India and Pakistan, which have fought two wars over Kashmir since independence from Britain in 1947, are scheduled to resume long-stalled official talks on Friday in New Delhi. Trade is a key item on the agenda.
"We (India and South Africa)...wanted to cooperate as members of the Indian Ocean Rim Association, which means a great deal for the development of our respective countries," Mandela said.
An Indian Ocean Rim Association for Regional Cooperation was recently formed by 14 nations including India and South Africa, whose economies are among the strongest in the rim.
Mandela said India and South Africa will sign during his visit a declaration seeking democratic reforms in the United Nations and the Commonwealth group of former British colonies.
Mandela, on his second official visit to India, said he would also discuss efforts to strengthen the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) of developing nations.
Foreign ministers of the Non-Aligned Movement nations are scheduled to meet in New Delhi on April 7 and 8.
Mandela first visited India in 1990 to receive the Bharat Ratna award, the country's highest civilian honour. His first official visit was in 1995.

Bilateral trade between the two nations rose to $600 million in 1996 from $80 million in 1993, when they restored diplomatic ties. It is poised to cross $1.0 billion in 1997, according to Indian foreign ministry statistics.
